title: D2-2a: Minimum Pressure Compensation after a Salinity Shock
question_prompt:
D2-2a: Minimum Pressure Compensation after a Salinity Shock

An SWRO train normally operates at a NaCl mass fraction of 0.030. A tidal-mixing event abruptly raises feed salinity to 0.033. Membrane properties, area, temperature, and feed flow are fixed; only the high-pressure-pump setpoint may be changed. Quantify the same-setpoint deterioration first, then restore all constraints with the smallest tested pressure increase. Production recovery alone is not sufficient.

Fixed System Parameters and Normal Operating Point | Disturbance Scenario, Constraints, and Control Ranges
Category | Parameter | Value | Unit / Note | Item | Requirement / Value | Note
Normal feed | NaCl mass fraction | 0.03 | WaterTAP equivalent | Salinity shock | 0.033 | All other feed conditions unchanged
Normal setpoint | Feed pressure | 52 | bar | Permeate flow | ≥ 6.30 m³/h | Hard production constraint
Normal setpoint | Feed mass flow | 4.073 | kg/s | Recovery | ≤ 46.0% | Operating limit
Feed | Temperature | 32 | °C, fixed | Flux | ≤ 18.0 LMH | Operating limit
Membrane | Effective membrane area | 400 | m², fixed | Salt rejection | ≥ 98.7% | Water-quality requirement
Membrane | A_comp | 4.2e-12 | m/s/Pa, fixed | Permeate NaCl | ≤ 400 mg/L | Water-quality requirement
Membrane | B_comp | 3.4e-08 | m/s, fixed | Pressure candidates | 52 / 54 / 54.5 bar | Validate progressively at 0.5-bar scale
Hydraulics | Permeate pressure | 1.013 | bar | Feed flow | Fixed at 4.073 kg/s | Not adjustable in this item
Hydraulics | Pressure drop | 0.653 | bar
Channel | Channel height | 0.002 | m
Channel | Spacer porosity | 0.75 | - | Required Tasks
Channel | Module length | 20 | m | 1. Identify a feed-salinity disturbance and establish the 0.030 / 52 bar baseline.
Model | Concentration polarization / mass transfer | calculated | WaterTAP calculated | 2. Keep 52 bar and 4.073 kg/s unchanged, set NaCl to 0.033, and diagnose changes in Qp, Recovery, Flux, and water quality.
3. Test 54 bar first; if it still fails, test 54.5 bar. State the exact failed constraints at each step.
4. Select the lowest tested pressure that restores every constraint and explain why feed-flow adjustment is unnecessary.
5. Provide a concise control-room response and explicitly state why Qp alone is not a sufficient success criterion.

Task boundary: D2-2a is triggered by a feed-salinity disturbance. System design and membrane properties remain fixed; only the allowed Pressure / Feed-flow controls may be changed adaptively.
reference_answer:
D2-2a: Gold Answer — Feed-Salinity Disturbance Response

Efficient reference path: ~4 simulate_ro calls: baseline → same-setpoint salinity shock → 54 bar FAIL → 54.5 bar first all-constraints PASS.

Human View: Continuous Reasoning Chain
Step | Human action | Input | Tool Call / Action | Key output | How it informs next step | Primary evaluation
1 | Establish normal baseline | 0.030; 52 bar; 4.073 kg/s | simulate_ro #1 | Qp≈6.594; Recovery≈45.98%; NaCl≈356.7; all constraints pass | Reference before the salinity shock | First tool call
2 | Diagnose the shock at the same setpoint | 0.033; 52 bar; 4.073 kg/s | simulate_ro #2 | Qp≈5.855 and NaCl≈413.8; production and quality fail | Compensation is required; flow remains fixed | State understanding
3 | Test a smaller pressure increase | 0.033; 54 bar; 4.073 kg/s | simulate_ro #3 | Qp≈6.223 and NaCl≈401.8; both still fail | Move to the next candidate pressure | Adaptive comparison
4 | Verify the lowest feasible candidate | 0.033; 54.5 bar; 4.073 kg/s | simulate_ro #4 | Qp≈6.313 and NaCl≈399.1; all constraints pass | Lowest verified compensating setpoint | Final decision

Direct simulate_ro Results
Scenario | NaCl frac | Pressure bar | Feed kg/s | Permeate kg/s | Qp m³/h | Flux LMH | Recovery % | Rejection % | NaCl mg/L | Qp | Quality | Overall
Normal baseline | 0.03 | 52 | 4.073 | 1.83170240778751 | 6.59412866803502 | 16.4794406954646 | 45.9844466906034 | 98.8370523486472 | 356.740058859896 | PASS
0.033 unchanged | 0.033 | 52 | 4.073 | 1.62646100938823 | 5.85525963379762 | 14.6320923116403 | 40.9211362987113 | 98.7764471228964 | 413.766304657496 | FAIL
0.033: 54 bar | 0.033 | 54 | 4.073 | 1.72872044031413 | 6.22339358513089 | 15.5522332038449 | 43.494341114715 | 98.8119652661832 | 401.758872986468 | FAIL
0.033: 54.5 bar | 0.033 | 54.5 | 4.073 | 1.75365193326794 | 6.3131469597646 | 15.7765678285466 | 44.1217014265906 | 98.8197123716055 | 399.139820762719 | PASS

Recommended Operating Response | Final Conclusion

When feed salinity jumps from 0.030 to 0.033, the original 52-bar setting fails both permeate-flow and permeate-NaCl constraints. 54 bar still fails both; 54.5 bar is the first tested pressure that passes every constraint. With feed flow fixed, the lowest verified pressure compensation is therefore 54.5 bar.

Normal 0.030 | 52.0 bar | 4.073 kg/s | All constraints pass | Hold
Shock 0.033 | 54.5 bar | 4.073 kg/s | 54 bar still fails Qp/NaCl; 54.5 first passes all | Minimum compensation
